newsitem.title: USA: Lockheed loses round in MFS contract dispute.
newsitem.headline: Lockheed loses round in MFS contract dispute.

text.p: A Delaware judge handed Lockheed Martin Corp another defeat in its effort to overturn a $500 million contract for electronic toll collection awarded to WorldCom Inc unit MFS Technologies Inc in March.
In an opinion released to Reuters Friday, Vice Chancellor Bernard Balick dismissed Lockheed's lawsuit against the Delaware Department of Transportation.

Lockheed had alleged that Delaware violated state law by delegating its authority in a "flawed" procurement process to the New Jersey Turnpike Authority, the lead agency in a tri-state consortium that also includes New York.
Balick said the Delaware agency had complied with the law and that "Delaware's interest is protected by the memorandum of understanding" among the consortium members.

The decision denies Lockheed's request to see documents related to the bidding process in which only Lokheed and MFS participated. But Balick did not rule on Lockheed's related allegation that a revenue-generating fiber optic option was introduced too late in the bidding process for Lockheed to act on it.
"Lockheed Martin has an adequate remedy for its claims of improprieties in the procurement process and must seek discovery relating to those claims in New Jersey," Balick said.
Lockheed has administrative claims pending against the New Jersey Turnpike Authority and has said it will appeal any denial of those claims to a New Jersey court.
